raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: Temporal Graph Networks (TGNs) is a generic, efficient framework for deep learning on dynamic graphs represented as sequences of timed events, combining memory modules and graph-based operators to capture temporal dependencies.
overlaps: Models dynamic graphs as sequences (of timed events), similar to GSAERU's modeling of dynamic graphs as sequences of snapshots
Focuses on dynamic/temporal graph representation learning
Aims to be computationally efficient for dynamic graph learning
differences: Uses memory modules and graph-based operators rather than graph summarization to compress the graph
Does not use a graph autoencoder for node representation learning
Does not explicitly use a recurrent neural network for temporal dependency modeling
Does not target large-scale graph compression via summarization

sources.title: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs
sources.quote: we present Temporal Graph Networks (TGNs), a generic, efficient framework for deep learning on dynamic graphs represented as sequences of timed events.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Inductive Representation Learning on Temporal Graphs
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: Temporal Graph Attention (TGAT) layer for inductive representation learning on temporal graphs, using self-attention to aggregate temporal-topological neighborhood features and functional time encoding.
overlaps: Focuses on temporal graph representation learning
Captures time-feature interactions and temporal patterns in dynamic graphs
differences: Uses self-attention mechanism rather than graph summarization for compression
Does not use a graph autoencoder for node representation learning
Does not use a recurrent neural network for temporal dependency modeling
Does not explicitly compress large-scale graphs

sources.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Temporal Graphs
sources.quote: We propose the temporal graph attention (TGAT) layer to efficiently aggregate temporal-topological neighborhood features as well as to learn the time-feature interactions.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: AGL is a scalable, fault-tolerant, and integrated system for GNN training and inference on large-scale graphs, using k-hop neighborhood generation and MapReduce-based message passing.
overlaps: Targets large-scale graph machine learning
Addresses scalability challenges in GNN training
differences: Uses k-hop neighborhood generation rather than graph summarization for compression
Does not use a graph autoencoder for node representation learning
Does not model dynamic/temporal graphs
Does not use a recurrent neural network for temporal dependencies

sources.title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
sources.quote: we design AGL, a scalable, fault-tolerance and integrated system, with fully-functional training and inference for GNNs.
